dialect.detail: TI-990 minicomputer COBOL; SOURCE-COMPUTER and OBJECT-COMPUTER both specify TI-990. Uses ISAM-style START/READ NEXT with alternate keys, COPY-based file definitions, and WRITE AFTER ADVANCING — consistent with a TI-990 or similar minicomputer COBOL environment.

purpose.domain_detail: Newspaper/periodical distribution — generates a Trenton (NJ) newspaper returns report listing dealer return quantities by day of week, output as a CSV file.
purpose.summary: Reads newspaper returns data from indexed files (WNR, WNA, WNK), accumulates daily return counts (Mon–Sun) per dealer for specific title numbers (049, 149, 249, 349, 449, 549), then writes a CSV output file with dealer name, address, phone, and per-day return totals. The output filename includes the issue date and is written to a fixed directory path.

notable_features: ISAM file access with START KEY GREATER and READ NEXT
Six COPY statements for file definitions and SELECT clauses
CSV output generated by replacing commas/periods/apostrophes via INSPECT and then inserting comma delimiters into FILLER fields
HERE label used as paragraph prefix on multiple MOVE statements (unusual label reuse)
No COMP-3 usage despite numeric accumulators
Commented-out test path and alternate filename variants
verdict.notes: The 'HERE' label appearing multiple times on consecutive lines is unusual — in standard COBOL a paragraph name can only appear once; this may be a TI-990 dialect extension or a coding quirk that the compiler tolerates. The program references FILLER1–FILLER15 by name, which is non-standard (FILLERs are normally anonymous) but supported by some compilers. Overall the code appears to be genuine production batch code for a newspaper distribution system.
